title: autotune: default batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ CLI
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost for common workloads by shipping safer defaults for batching and prefix caching, add a set of recommended quantization profiles for popular families, and expose unit-economics tooling so SREs and product engineers can quickly see cost impact. This PR implements: 1) Autotune defaults: new heuristics to pick per-model default batch_size, max_concurrent_requests, and cache policy based on historical request-size distribution and latency SLOs. 2) Quantization profiles: curated profiles (fp16 / int8 / int4 variants) with fallbacks and compatibility metadata for each model in the catalog. 3) Unit-econ CLI: a small command-line tool and HTTP endpoint that takes a route + traffic mix and returns estimated token cost, latency P95, and recommended config (batching/quant/profile). 4) Telemetry and CI: added new metrics (unit_econ_estimate, autotune_suggestions) and unit tests + integration tests in perf-canary job. Rollout plan: feature-flag behind autotune_defaults; gradual rollout to 10% of traffic with canary comparisons against existing defaults. Checklist: - [x] design doc in Linear ENG-1093 - [x] unit tests and integration tests - [x] metrics + dashboards updated - [x] docs + CLI help text - [x] feature-flagged rollout - [x] backwards-compatible config schema changes Backwards compatibility: config schema added optional fields with defaults so existing deployments keep prior behavior. Related: ENG-1093, ENG-1120.
commits: feat(autotune): heuristics for batching and prefix caching based on request distribution
chore(models): add quantization profiles metadata for t5, llama-family, and redwood-curated models
feat(uecon): add unit-econ CLI and lightweight HTTP estimate endpoint
test(autotune): add integration test exercising canary rollout and fallback behavior
docs: update runtime and console docs for new autotune defaults and unit-econ tool
ci: add perf-canary job to validate cost/latency regressions
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and caching, curated quantization profiles, and a unit-economics CLI. No breaking changes; feature gated behind `autotune_defaults` flag.
comments: Jacob Lin: High level LGTM. Two requests: can we limit the initial rollout to 5% until we validate int4 quality on long-context datasets? Also please add a dashboard tile for unit_econ_estimate.

Asha Patel: Responding - agree on cautious rollout. Updated perf-canary to run the int4 quality job and set initial rollout to 5% with a follow-up to 25% after metrics look good. Added dashboard tile in perf-canary job (see perf-canary/jobs/uecon_validation.yml).
Priya Rao: Nit: rename heuristics.py -> policy_selector.py for clarity. Also add a short migration note for operators who pin config.json.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for heuristics and CLI. Integration test validates canary fallback to prior defaults under SLO violation. Perf-canary job runs with synthetic mixes (chat, single-turn, long-context); observed median cost reduction 12% for chat-heavy workloads and no P95 regressions on gated rollout.
deploy_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 weeks with automatic rollback on cost or P95 regressions. Post-rollout: enable recommendations in console with opt-out per-route.
notes: This PR centralizes cost-saving defaults and tooling; teams should evaluate per-workload before enabling int4 profiles in production. Ops: monitor autotune_suggestions and unit_econ_estimate metrics.
merge_notes: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Rollout started using feature flag `autotune_defaults`. Perf-canary validated estimates before widening the rollout.
